title: What a Spreadsheet Is
description: The Spreadsheet Service Database holds the full record for What a Spreadsheet Is. A spreadsheet is a grid of rows and columns where numbers and words are kept in cells, and where formulas can add the numbers up by themselves. Change one number and every total that depends on it changes at once. It is used for budgets, lists, and accounts, anywhere that numbers must be added, compared, and kept in order. title: Typing Numbers and Words
description: The Spreadsheet Service Database holds the full record for Typing Numbers and Words. A cell holds one thing: a number, a word, or a formula. A number typed with a comma or a pound sign is still a number to the sheet, while a word that looks like a number is treated as text and cannot be added up. title: Copying a Formula Down a Column
description: The Spreadsheet Service Database holds the full record for Copying a Formula Down a Column. A formula copied down a column changes its cell names to match each new row, so =SUM(A1:A5) in row one becomes the matching sum for row two, and so on. This is how one formula fills a whole column of totals. The writer writes the formula once, checks it once, and lets the sheet repeat it.
